analysis.title: Retail Sales Growth Slowed in October; Industrial Production Down Slightly
key_insights: Retail sales rose 0.2% in October after gains of 1.5% in August and 0.8% in September. The slowdown came from falling auto sales and a smaller rise in gasoline prices.
Sales at gasoline stations rose 3.7% in August, 6.0% in September and 1.5% in October, which drove much of the earlier gains.
Motor vehicle and parts sales fell 1.6% in October. Retail sales excluding autos rose 0.6% and excluding autos and gasoline rose 0.5%.
Control sales (excluding autos, gasoline, food service and building materials) rose 0.6% in October, in line with the 2026 trend.

Retail sales were up 6.8% y/y in October, with sales excluding autos up 8.1% and excluding autos and gasoline up 5.9%. These are the strongest growth rates since late 2022 or early 2023. Control sales were up 5.6% y/y, the largest gain in four years.

Consumer sentiment (University of Michigan) hit its second-lowest level ever in October and rose slightly in November, but spending data does not show the weakness. Purchases are rising faster than inflation.

PNC attributes spending strength to a solid labor market (unemployment 4.1%, average job gains above 70,000 a month this year versus 12,000 last year) and to wealth gains from the stock market, particularly among high-income consumers.
PNC forecasts 2026 holiday sales growth of about 7% before price adjustment and about 6% after, since prices for holiday goods are up less than 1% y/y. Most of the growth is online.
Industrial production fell 0.4% in October, the largest monthly decline since January. Utilities output fell 4.3% after a September surge tied to hot weather, and mining fell 0.8%.
Manufacturing output rose 0.3% in October and has risen every month this year except August. High-tech goods production rose 2.1%, tied to the AI buildout.
Industrial production was up 2.1% y/y and manufacturing up 2.2%. Manufacturing is slightly below its early 2023 post-pandemic peak and 9% below its late 2007 high.
Capacity utilization fell to 76.4% from 76.8%. Manufacturing capacity utilization rose to 76.0% from 75.9%. Both are low historically, indicating little price pressure from capacity constraints.

PNC expects manufacturing output to keep rising gradually through 2026 and 2027, with high interest rates limiting the expansion. Elevated energy prices, high tariffs and strong tech demand are causing goods inflation in late 2026.

sector_views.rationale: Manufacturing output should rise gradually through 2027 on economic growth and tech demand, but high interest rates limit the expansion.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Slowdown from +1.5% in August and +0.8% in September, due to lower auto sales and a smaller gasoline price increase.
Underlying sales remained solid when autos are excluded.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Feeds nominal consumer spending in real GDP, consistent with the 2026 trend.
Strongest growth since late 2022 or early 2023.
Largest monthly decline since January, driven by utilities and mining.
Manufacturing has risen every month in 2026 except August.
Down from 76.8% in September. Low on a historical basis, so little price pressure from capacity limits.
About 6% after adjusting for prices, with most growth online.

risk_factors: High interest rates will limit manufacturing expansion.
Elevated energy prices, high tariffs and strong demand for tech goods are adding to goods inflation.
Consumer sentiment is near record lows, though it has not yet shown up in spending.

tension_points.bull_case: Spending is rising faster than inflation, supported by a solid labor market (unemployment 4.1%, job gains above 70,000 a month) and stock market wealth gains among high-income consumers. Control sales are up 5.6% y/y.
tension_points.bear_case: University of Michigan sentiment hit its second-lowest level ever in October and midterm results signal widespread displeasure about the economy, with high interest rates and rising inflation as headwinds.

theme_stances.key_argument: Consumer spending continues to hold up despite rising inflation and high interest rates.
theme_stances.evidence: Consumer spending continues to hold up despite rising inflation and high interest rates.
